Header:
Date: 2026-07-08

Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood AE)
- Ethan Park (Redwood SE)
- Sofia Ramirez (Blue Ridge, Head of ML)
- Daniel Lee (Blue Ridge, Platform Eng)
- Priya Singh (Blue Ridge, Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood model catalog and how to pick portfolio variants for a latency-sensitive financial chat use case. Focus on bench interpretation, compatibility with our infra (GKE -> private VPC option), and required security artifacts. Customer asked for shortlist + benchmark plan and details on private deployment (KMS, SOC 2, audit logs).

Topics:
- Catalog browsing and filters (size, task-fit, quantization support)
- Benchmarks: p99 latency, tokens/sec, RLHF/Instr tuning impact
- Compatibility matrix: kernel/hardware fit, quantized support, KV cache footprint
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
- Security: KMS, SSO, audit logging, data residency

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. Quick intros — we're Maya (AE) and Ethan (SE) from Redwood.
[00:12] Sofia: Hi, Sofia here, thanks, really keen to see how you map models to our latency targets.
[00:15] Daniel: Daniel — mainly interested in infra constraints, we run GKE in us-east-1 and want private connectivity.
[00:20] Priya: Priya, security — SOC two requirements, KMS, and auditability are must-haves.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Agenda: quick catalog tour in the console, show filters and shortlist, then Ethan will go through bench results and the compatibility matrix. We'll finish with Q&A and next steps.
[00:45] Ethan: okay I'm sharing my screen now. bit dotly slash rwd-catalog-demo — apologies if the link sh- the slides are in the deck.
[01:15] Ethan: On the left is the model catalog — we surface model meta like architecture, recommended sequence length, and our perf profiles. Note: some of the model names get truncated in the UI, so do ask if something looks off.
[01:40] Sofia: Could you show how you filter for quantization-friendly models? We need 4-bit or 8-bit runs for cost reasons.
[01:50] Ethan: Yep — filter -> "quantization support" -> 8-bit int8/4-bit q4_hp. We also tag models that are known to work well with our kernel set — that's the compatibility bit.
[02:10] Daniel: When you say kernel set, is that the vendor kernel mapping — like cuBLAS vs Triton kernels? We use A100 pods today.
[02:18] Ethan: Good question — we map to optimized kernels (nvfuser/cuBLAS/Triton/MLC) and show a compatibility score. For A100 the typical sweet spot is these medium-sized dense models — for very large seq lengths you get KV cache pressure.
[02:40] Maya: I'll pause here — real quick qualification: what's your target p95/p99 latency and acceptable cost per 1k tokens?
[02:52] Sofia: Target p95 ~ 250ms for short chats (<=256 tokens), p99 under 500ms ideally. Cost — we'd like to keep hosted inference under $0.02 per 1k tokens but we can stretch for dedicated if latency needs it.
[03:08] Ethan: Okay that helps. We'll recommend a portfolio with a low-latency variant for short queries and a cost-savvy fallback model. The catalog supports routing policies to implement that.
[03:30] Priya: On data residency — all inference must remain in our VPC, no customer data leaves our network. Is private deployment an option?
[03:38] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging. We'll share the VPC checklist and the KMS integration doc after this call.
[03:55] Daniel: For POC — we'd like to run a small benchmark against our sample prompts. How are your benchmarks run (real-time streaming vs batched)?
[04:05] Ethan: We run both. Bench spreadsheets in the repo include streaming p99 and batched throughput. For chat use cases, streaming p95/p99 matter more. We'll run a targeted bench on your prompts to get apples-to-apples numbers.
[04:30] Sofia: Could you explain the compatibility matrix — what factors go into the score?
[04:35] Ethan: Sure — it's a weighted score across architecture match (decoder/encoder-decoder), kernel availability, quantization friendliness, KV cache RAM footprint, expected throughput on the selected hardware, and historical quality signals from our evals. There can be false positives — you should look at the bench numbers and the model's instruction tuning lineage.
[04:58] Maya: Example: for a 7B open model we might get a score of 87 on A100, but the 13B quantized q4 version might be 86 with higher mem but better instr-following.
[05:20] Priya: Are the evals reproducible? We need test artifacts for our compliance team.
[05:25] Ethan: Yes, we attach runbooks and the prompts used, plus raw logs when under NDA. For the POC we can provide those artifacts.
[05:45] Daniel: Any support for hardware other than NVidia? We have a small fleet of Habana nodes in a separate cluster.
[05:52] Ethan: We have limited compatibility mapping for Habana and for some GCP TPU types. The matrix flags unsupported hardware. If Habana is critical we can run an offline kernel compatibility pass.
[06:15] Maya: okay i'm going to demo the shortlist flow — Ethan will annotate Qs about the bench.
[06:25] Ethan: here i add a filter: task=chat, tokens <=512, quantization=4-bit or 8-bit, latency-focused. The UI returns a set of candidates with perf bands: latency average, p95, cost estimate.
[06:45] Sofia: The cost estimate — is that per-token or per-inference?
[06:50] Ethan: Per 1k tokens by default, and we show cost-per-request approximation based on your prompt/response length distribution if you upload a profile.
[07:10] Daniel: The KV cache footprint — can you show an example for 1024 context? We're tight on GPU RAM.
[07:18] Ethan: Sure. For model X-7B q4 the KV cache is about 2.1GB for 1024; for X-13B q4 it's ~4.3GB. Those numbers are approximate — exact depends on tokenizer and sequence.
[07:40] Sofia: Are those numbers measured on A100 or T4ish hardware?
[07:44] Ethan: Measured on A100 40GB baseline. For T4 or smaller, the effective available memory and kernel performance differ.
[07:55] Priya: On encryption — if we use Redwood Private, does Redwood manage the KMS keys or can we bring our own?
[08:02] Maya: You can bring your own KMS/HSM. We integrate with cloud KMS and support customer-managed keys; we'll show the integration steps in the doc we send.
[08:20] Daniel: Any automatic routing for fallbacks? Like if the low-latency pool is saturated, we want to fallback to a slightly slower model without erroring.
[08:28] Ethan: Yes — routing policies support priority lists, model variants, and cost-based fallback. We expose that in the Console as per-route policies and you can set soft SLOs.
[08:50] Maya: Now to benches — Ethan, could you show a bench example where we compare three models across latency and cost?
[08:58] Ethan: Pulling up the bench sheet — here we have ModelA-7B, ModelB-7B-qt, ModelC-13B-q4. The sheet shows median latency, p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k. Note some of our earlier sheets had transcription typos — "Model B" got called "Model Bee" in the header, ignore that.
[09:30] Sofia: The instruction-tuned variants — how much does that shift latency?
[09:35] Ethan: Instruction tuning typically increases prompt length which can change token counts; execution time per token is similar but end-to-end latency can increase due to longer responses. We capture that in the bench by running representative prompts.
[09:55] Daniel: About the benchmark environment — can we run those benches in our env?
[10:00] Ethan: Absolutely. For POC we'll run both: your env (private VPC) and our hosted to compare. We'll provide the bench harness (python tool + tokenizer) so you can reproduce locally.
[10:25] Priya: Are audit logs available for inference calls and key lifecycle events? We need retention for 1 year.
[10:32] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports audit log retention and we can export logs to your SIEM. We'll align retention windows per contract.
[10:45] Sofia: Are there any known model hallucination regressions when you quantize to q4? We worry about quality drop.
[10:53] Ethan: There can be regressions; our Optimize toolkit runs quality monitors and will flag regressions on known prompts. For critical prompts we recommend a small eval set to run against quantized candidates before rollout.
[11:15] Daniel: Can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[11:20] Maya: Yes — the Console supports pinned versions, canary percentages, and auto-fallback if quality monitors spike.
[11:35] Sofia: Regarding pricing — you mentioned reserved capacity for dedicated pools. What's the typical commit for a small pilot?
[11:42] Maya: For Dedicated, smallest reserved pool is typically 4 GPU equivalent for monthly commit; for pilots we often do a short-term reserved or a burstable add-on. We'll send pricing examples.
[12:00] Ethan: going back to the compatibility matrix — note we also surface kernel mismatches as warnings. If a model uses a fused attention kernel we don't fully support on older drivers, the matrix flags it and we recommend a fallback model.
[12:25] Daniel: If we choose private deployment, is there an on-prem/offline install? We have a secure cluster that cannot touch the public internet.
[12:33] Maya: We have an on-prem package that can be air-gapped; it requires coordination for model weights licensing and initial bootstrap. We'll need your infra team to sign an NDA to exchange weights.
[12:55] Priya: Regarding licensing — any restrictions on redistributing model weights? Some open models carry specific licenses.
[13:03] Ethan: Correct — the catalog shows license metadata. For certain models you need to accept model-specific terms; we annotate that in the UI.
[13:20] Sofia: We'd like to see a recommended portfolio — a primary low-latency model, a fallback, and an archival cost-saver. Could you demo how you assemble that?
[13:28] Ethan: Sure — create a "portfolio" in the UI, drag three models: low-latency q4-7B, fallback q4-13B, archival 7B-8bit. Then set routing weights and a rule: if p95 > 400ms or queue size>5 then route to fallback.
[13:55] Daniel: How granular are routing rules? Can we route based on token length or user tier?
[14:02] Ethan: Yes — route by headers, token counts, and customer tier. We also support A/Bing and canary flags.
[14:20] Maya: Quick interjection — noted that Daniel wants token-length routing. We'll include a sample policy in the POC runbook.
[14:32] Sofia: On the sample prompts — we'll upload 3 classes: short chat, doc-summarize, and financial-rules QA. We expect different model behavior per class.
[14:45] Ethan: Perfect — that will help us pick the shortlist and run focused evals.
[15:05] Priya: Another security Q: does Redwood store request/response text by default?
[15:12] Maya: For hosted we store minimal logs; for Private you control retention. We can configure redaction and retention policies.
[15:30] Daniel: About monitoring — do you have token-level breakdowns for cost tracing?
[15:35] Ethan: Yes — the Console shows token-level cost per model and per route, plus tracing to individual calls when debug mode is enabled.
[15:55] Sofia: OK this is helpful — can you walk through a specific bench comparison?
[16:00] Ethan: Sure — pulling the bench: Model L7-q4 median=120ms, p95=230ms, cost $0.018/1k. Model M13-q4 median=180ms, p95=360ms, cost $0.030/1k. Model archival 7-8bit median=210ms but much cheaper for long-form.
[16:30] Sofia: So it looks like L7 is within our p95 target for most short chats. The p99 spikes we saw earlier — are those due to batching or GC events?
[16:38] Ethan: p99 can be influenced by queueing and long-tail hardware events; we mitigate with pre-warmed pools and continuous batching policies.
[16:55] Daniel: On the pre-warmed pools — any warmup cost? If we keep warm workers idle, that's another cost.
[17:02] Maya: Yes there's a tradeoff — warm pools cost standby GPU time. Our Optimize tool suggests warm sizes based on traffic profiles; we can run sims for your expected load.
[17:20] Sofia: Could you run a sim for our expected 200 qps peak with 60/40 short/long?
[17:26] Ethan: We'll schedule that as part of the POC; add it to action items.
[17:40] Priya: For the POC, will you require us to run an agent in our VPC or do you host a connector?
[17:48] Ethan: For Private we run a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC and lightweight agents to manage workers. For on-prem airgap there's an installer.
[18:05] Daniel: We have autoscaler constraints in our k8s cluster — can Redwood's autoscaling integrate with KEDA or our cluster-autoscaler?
[18:12] Ethan: We expose hooks; many customers use cluster-autoscaler + KEDA integration. We'll share examples.
[18:30] Sofia: Any red flags you'd call out for our use case?
[18:34] Ethan: Biggest things: KV cache memory on larger contexts, and quantization quality regressions. We'll surface these in the compatibility matrix and recommend a short eval.
[18:50] Maya: quick recap — we'll send: catalog export, shortlist + compatibility matrix, bench harness, security pack, and pricing examples.
[19:03] Sofia: Sounds good. A couple of clarifying Qs: can you do tokenization for multilingual prompts? We need Spanish and Portuguese support.
[19:12] Ethan: Yes — models vary on tokenizer coverage; the catalog shows language coverage. For multilingual you'd pick models with broader vocab.
[19:28] Daniel: Any partner integrations for observability — we use Datadog.
[19:33] Maya: We have Datadog exporters and SIEM integrations for logs.
[19:40] Priya: Final security ask — can we get a sample contract clause for data handling?
[19:45] Maya: We'll include example contract language in the security pack.
[19:55] Sofia: Ok next steps — we want the shortlist and an invite to POC kickoff.
[20:01] Maya: we'll target the week of 2026-07-20 for POC kickoff; i'll propose times.
[20:10] Ethan: i'll own the compatibility matrix and the bench run.
[20:15] Daniel: i'll loop infra and schedule the kickoff.
[20:25] Priya: i'll confirm KMS and compliance needs.
[20:35] Maya: Great — any more questions?
[20:40] Sofia: One last thing — competitor question: how is Redwood different from Anthropic or Vertex for these workloads?
[20:49] Ethan: In short: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, more production tooling around cost/perf controls, and stronger observability for routing and canary rollouts. We focus on inference economics.
[21:10] Sofia: Thanks, that's helpful.
[21:15] Maya: ok we'll stop screen-share and I'll drop links in the follow-up.
[21:20] Daniel: thanks all.
